name: Pisang Peak Climbing
sub_region: Manang District, Gandaki Province (Damodar Himal per NMA; Annapurna Conservation Area)

difficulty.notes: Standard route is the south-west/west ridge: Base Camp ~4,380 m, High Camp ~5,400 m on a rocky shoulder, then a steep, exposed snow/ice ridge (45-50 degrees) to the summit pyramid with fixed ropes on exposed sections. ~700 m vertical on summit day. Crampons, ice axe, harness, ascender required. [s5][s6][s7]

duration_days.basis: full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu, jeep in and out via Besisahar
duration_days.notes: Short version drives Kathmandu-Chame and back out from Pisang. Longer versions combine the climb with the Annapurna Circuit over Thorong La (15-18 days) for better acclimatisation. [s6][s8]

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation, training and preparation day at Pisang

itinerary.notes: Steep rocky ridge, snow possible; rope/crampon training. [s5][s6]

itinerary.route: High Camp - Pisang Peak summit (6,091 m) - descend to Base Camp/Pisang
itinerary.notes: Pre-dawn start; turnaround at guide's discretion. [s5][s6]

best_seasons.notes: High Camp route can be snow-covered from late autumn to early spring. [s5] NMA royalty is lower in autumn (USD 175) than spring (USD 350). [s1]

permits.name: NMA peak climbing permit (royalty) - Pisang Peak 6,091 m
permits.fee: Per foreign climber: USD 350 spring (Mar-May), USD 175 autumn (Sep-Nov), USD 175 winter (Dec-Feb), USD 175 summer (Jun-Aug)

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per foreign national (SAARC NPR 1,000), tax included

guide_requirements: Climbing permits are arranged through a registered agency; climbs are led by a licensed climbing guide. The 2025 sixth amendment to mountaineering regulations requires at least one mountain guide per team on mountains other than 8,000 m peaks. [s10] Licensed trekking-guide rule applies on the ACAP approach. [s11]

flights: Optional exit Jomsom - Pokhara ~20-25 min if continuing over Thorong La [s12]
drives: Kathmandu - Besisahar - Chame by bus/jeep (long day) [s6]
logistics.notes: Teahouses to Pisang; tented camps at Base Camp and High Camp. Max 15 members per NMA permit team. [s2][s5]

highlights: Summit views of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu and the Chulu peaks [s5][s8]
Approachable 6,000 m objective on the Annapurna Circuit [s6]
Can be combined with Thorong La [s8]
risks: Steep exposed summit ridge (45-50 degrees) requiring fixed-rope technique [s7]
Rapid ascent profile in the short itinerary (Pisang 3,300 m to High Camp 5,400 m in two days) [s6]
Snow and ice conditions vary by season [s5]

acclimatization.notes: Short itinerary has one acclimatisation day at Pisang; circuit-combined versions acclimatise more gradually. [s6][s8]

unverified: NMA garbage deposit amount: TAAN/operators say USD 250; DoT schedule lists USD 500 for peaks below 6,500 m in the Annapurna range (that schedule may apply only to DoT-administered peaks).
Technical grade varies between PD+ and AD by source.
Whether the sixth-amendment 'one mountain guide per team' rule formally covers NMA peaks.
